79231.subject: SEC, CFTC Say They'll Write the Crypto Rulebook Without Congress
79231.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[The SEC and CFTC](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/sec-and-cftc-chairmen-say-they-will-write-crypto-rules-without-clarity-act)**[ chairmen said they will write crypto rules without the CLARITY Act](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/sec-and-cftc-chairmen-say-they-will-write-crypto-rules-without-clarity-act)

* **[Bitcoin](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-round-trips-fed-rate-increase-zcash-sep-16-2026)**[ round-tripped the first Fed rate increase since 2023 as Zcash ran to $1,383](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-round-trips-fed-rate-increase-zcash-sep-16-2026)

* **[Circle](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/circle-launches-arc-mainnet-with-blackrock-dtcc-and-visa-producing-blocks)**[ opened Arc's mainnet with BlackRock, DTCC and Visa producing blocks](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/circle-launches-arc-mainnet-with-blackrock-dtcc-and-visa-producing-blocks)

* **[Kraken's parent](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/kraken-parent-plans-permissioned-hyperliquid-perps-for-us-traders)**[ wants permissioned Hyperliquid perps for U.S. traders](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/kraken-parent-plans-permissioned-hyperliquid-perps-for-us-traders)

* **[Aave Labs](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/aave-avalanche-rwa-hub-usat-tokenized-collateral)**[ plans a tokenized-asset credit market on Avalanche with Tether's USA₮](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/aave-avalanche-rwa-hub-usat-tokenized-collateral)

The CFTC chairman posted his statement at 10:35 a.m. ET on Wednesday. The SEC chairman followed at 12:11 p.m. Michael Selig said the CFTC is "locked in and ready to ship its rules for the new frontier of finance." Paul Atkins said he had "been unequivocal: with or without legislation, we will act decisively within the SEC's statutory authority."

It’s the optimistic view many in the industry have tried taking after the Senate setback: Crypto can still get a regulatory framework in the U.S. without the bill. The SEC put Regulation Crypto Assets in the Federal Register on Aug. 21 with comments closing Oct. 20. Separately, Atkins named a transfer agent rule and a custody proposal. Meanwhile, the CFTC has sent 18 proposals to the Register since January, and the crypto market structure rule Selig has now described twice is absent from that list. And the question that clouds the picture is that the rules one agency chair writes can be unwritten by the next one.

**Read more below!**

79229.subject: 🟪 Monetary policy is going asymmetric
79229.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9f199753-ca31-4e3d-9435-5e12896ecff5/BD_NL_Banner_Heading.png?t=1781793903)
Caption: 

----------
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/3bd8a492-ff61-41db-a7f2-c821d481fd72/BD_NL_QuoteCircle.png?t=1781794162)
Caption: 

“If I seem unduly clear to you, you must have misunderstood what I said.”
_— Alan Greenspan_



----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f247dc88-557d-451e-959d-f1b7376671ea/unnamed.png?t=1789595063)
Caption: 

# Monetary policy is going asymmetric 

The stock market was down today because the FOMC “signaled the possibility of further policy tightening,” Bloomberg [reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-15/asian-stocks-to-edge-higher-as-traders-await-fed-markets-wrap?itm_source=record&itm_campaign=US_Stocks&itm_content=Today%E2%80%99s_Markets_Wrap-0).

Or because Chair Warsh “highlighted that the inflation risk wasn’t improving,” CNBC [said](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/15/stock-market-today-live-updates.html).

Or something else, maybe.

We can never know for sure why the market does what it does — because “the market” isn’t even a thing, really.

Saying the market went up or down for some identifiable reason is to anthropomorphize an abstract representation of millions of individual decisions, made for a million different reasons. Only some of which we can guess at.

Sometimes it’s easy to turn that process into a story, like today. Today’s story — rates up, markets down — is a standard one.

But it’s _only_ a story. I know this because I spent about two decades telling them. A large part of a trader’s job at an investment bank is coming up with plausible-sounding explanations for why a stock (or the market) went up or down that day.

I was very good at it! Only rarely did I resort to the last-ditch explanation of “more buyers than sellers” (or vice versa).

But AI is about to make this a lot harder.

Consider that part of the reason the market was down today may have been an expression on Chair Warsh’s face  — because even a look from the Fed chair can move markets.

Expressions of concern, stress, or unhappiness seem to have the greatest impact. “We find that investors adversely react to negative expressions revealed during the press conference,” one [study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304393223000740) found.

The researchers used facial recognition software and machine-learning algorithms to determine that, on average, the S&P 500 fell 0.53 basis points in the three minutes after a negative look from the Fed chair. Index volatility rose 3.8 basis points. 

“Market participants observing Chair's negative facial expressions during the FOMC
